failure_summary.description: Reply had no flight word (rooms/party size, bare 'Yes' to an attraction offer, hotel amenities), yet flight keys were re-filtered with an invented or earlier class/date, and old hotel kwargs were re-passed.
'That would be great' accepting 'Touristy attractions near your hotel' (no attractions key) produced filters instead of search_attractions + search_nearest.
In a multi-city trip, the attraction search was done for only one destination city instead of one per city.
Hotel without dates plus restaurants in a known city: output was only seek_information, with no search_restaurants.
'NV' was passed as city= instead of state= in search_attractions.

patch.reasoning: Three of six failures were spurious flight filters on replies with no flight word, so I tightened the existing flight-rule sentence rather than adding a gate. That edit also adds the rooms/party-size row. The DATE GATE is the first rule the agent reads, and it implied a lone seek_information, so it now says to search other searchable domains first. A short bullet under Rule 26 covers bare acceptance of an attraction offer (first search plus search_nearest) and one attraction search per destination city. A one-line hygiene fix makes two-letter state codes unmistakable. I deliberately avoided touching the Rule 2/17 'earlier constraint' clauses, because edits there were rejected in earlier steps.

edits.target: Conversely, when the last message is about hotels or restaurants, write no flight line.
edits.content: Conversely, when the user's LAST message has no flight word (an amenity, stars, neighborhood, a hotel budget, rooms or party size, a restaurant or attraction request, or a bare 'Yes' / 'That would be great'), write ZERO flight lines. A class or date named in an earlier turn is already in the flight keys' summaries and is never re-applied, and never invent a flight_class. A rooms / party-size reply ('M rooms and N people') is exactly `filter_hotels(prior_results=<most refined hotels key>, num_rooms=M, num_people=N)` + save, on hotels only.

edits.target: It is the whole output unless another requested domain is searchable (see 4b).
edits.content: First search every OTHER requested domain that is searchable (a restaurant or attraction request with a city known anywhere, e.g. 'hotel in Fresno for 5 ... also restaurants in the city' -> `restaurants = search_restaurants(city="Fresno")` + `save_to_cache(key="restaurants", value=restaurants)`), and put the single seek_information last. The seek_information is the whole output only when no other requested domain is searchable (see 4b).

edits.target: - Without a hotels key, 'near the hotel' needs no search_nearest. Just run the normal first search.
edits.content:
- A bare acceptance ('That would be great', 'Yes, that sounds amazing') of the assistant's offer of an attraction type or restaurants, when CACHE has NO key for that domain, is a FIRST SEARCH of it: type or cuisine copied from the assistant's last message, city = trip destination. If the offer said 'near your hotel' and a hotels key is cached: `attractions = search_attractions(city="<destination>", type=["<offered type>"])` + save 'attractions', then `h = get_results_from_cache(key="<most refined hotels key>")`, `nearest_hotels = search_nearest(hotels=h, attractions=attractions, groupBy="hotel")` + save. Never re-filter flights or hotels for such a reply.
- Multi-city trip (keys like first_/second_ flights and hotels): run the attraction (or restaurant) search once per destination city, saved as first_attractions and second_attractions, in the same block. Add search_nearest only when the offer said near/close to the hotel (one per city, using that city's hotels key).

edits.target: A US state or abbreviation ('OR', 'CA', 'Georgia', 'a trip to CA') goes in `state=`, never in `city=`.
edits.content: A US state or any two-letter state code ('NV', 'OR', 'CA', 'GA', 'Georgia', 'a trip to CA') goes in `state=`, never in `city=`; `city="NV"` is always wrong.
